title: Create a ticket manually
aliases: log a ticket for a phone call
open a ticket on behalf of a customer
body:
Use this when a customer contacts you by phone or in person.
1. Select **New ticket** at the top of the screen.
2. In **Requester**, start typing the customer's name or email and select them from the list.
3. Enter a **Subject** and a description of the issue.
4. Set the **Priority** and **Assignee** if needed.
5. Select **Submit as Open**.

title: Reply to a customer on a ticket
body:
1. Open the ticket from **Tickets** or a view.
2. Select **Reply** below the conversation.
3. Type your message. The reply goes to the requester and any CC recipients.
4. Choose a status from the **Submit as** menu.
5. Select **Send**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Add an internal note to a ticket
aliases: write a note only agents can see
add a comment for my team
body:
Internal notes are never sent to the requester.
1. Open the ticket.
2. Select **Add note** below the conversation.
3. Type your note. Use @ followed by a name to mention a colleague.
4. Select **Add note** to save it.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Assign a ticket to an agent
aliases: hand over a ticket to a colleague
body:
1. Open the ticket.
2. In the **Properties** panel, select the **Assignee** field.
3. Choose the agent from the list, or select **Take it** to assign the ticket to yourself.
4. Select **Save**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Assign a ticket to a group
aliases: send a ticket to a team
change the group on a ticket
route a ticket to another queue
body:
1. Open the ticket.
2. In the **Properties** panel, select the **Group** field.
3. Choose the group, such as **Billing** or **Technical Support**.
4. Leave **Assignee** blank to let the group pick it up, or choose an agent.
5. Select **Save**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Merge two tickets
aliases: merge a duplicate ticket into another
consolidate tickets from the same customer
body:
The duplicate ticket is closed after the merge.
1. Open the ticket you want to keep as the main ticket.
2. Select the **More actions** menu, then **Merge**.
3. Search for the duplicate ticket by number or subject and select it.
4. Choose whether to add the duplicate's comments as a public reply or an internal note.
5. Select **Merge tickets**.

title: Split a message into a new ticket
aliases: break out a reply into its own ticket
separate a second issue from a ticket
create a new ticket from a comment
body:
The original ticket stays as it is and links to the new one.
1. Open the ticket and find the message that raises the separate issue.
2. Select the **More** menu on that message, then **Create ticket from message**.
3. Review the subject and requester on the new ticket.
4. Select **Create ticket**.

title: Close a ticket
body:
Closed tickets are locked. Use a follow-up ticket if the customer writes in again.
1. Open the ticket.
2. Select **Reply** or **Add note** if you want to leave a final message.
3. Open the **Submit as** menu and select **Closed**.
4. Select **Send** or **Add note**.

title: Reopen a closed ticket
aliases: customer wrote back on a closed ticket
body:
Tickets that have been closed for more than 60 days cannot be reopened. Create a follow-up ticket instead.
1. Search for the ticket and open it.
2. Select **Reopen ticket** at the top of the page.
3. Choose **Open** or **Pending** as the new status.
4. Select **Confirm**.

title: Delete a ticket
body:
Deleted tickets stay in **Deleted tickets** for 30 days, then are removed permanently.
1. Open the ticket.
2. Select the **More actions** menu.
3. Select **Delete**.
4. Select **Delete ticket** to confirm.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Restore a deleted ticket
aliases: get a ticket back from the bin
I deleted a ticket by mistake
body:
You can restore a ticket within 30 days of deleting it. After that it is gone permanently.
1. Go to **Tickets**, then select **Deleted tickets**.
2. Find the ticket in the list.
3. Select **Restore** next to it.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Export tickets to CSV
aliases: get a CSV of all tickets
body:
Only admins can export ticket data.
1. Go to **Admin**, then **Data export**.
2. Select **Tickets**.
3. Choose a date range and the fields to include.
4. Select **Export to CSV**.
5. Open the email we send you and download the file within 48 hours.

title: Attach a file to a reply
aliases: add an attachment to a ticket
send a document to the customer
upload a file on a ticket
include a screenshot in a reply
body:
Each reply can include files up to 20 MB in total.
1. Open the ticket and select **Reply**.
2. Select the paperclip icon, or drag the file into the reply box.
3. Wait for the upload to finish.
4. Select **Send**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Add a CC recipient to a ticket
aliases: copy someone in on a ticket
include another person in the email
cc a colleague of the customer
body:
CC recipients receive all public replies on the ticket until you remove them.
1. Open the ticket and select **Reply**.
2. Select **CC** above the message box.
3. Enter the email address of the person to copy in.
4. Select **Send**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Follow a ticket
aliases: keep an eye on a ticket
body:
Followers receive an email each time the ticket is updated.
1. Open the ticket.
2. In the **Properties** panel, select **Followers**.
3. Select **Add me**, or search for a colleague's name to add them.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Update several tickets at once
body:
You can update up to 100 tickets at a time.
1. Open a view from **Views** and tick the checkbox next to each ticket you want to change.
2. Select **Bulk edit** at the top of the list.
3. Change the **Status**, **Priority**, **Group** or **Assignee**.
4. Select **Submit**.

title: Set a due date on a ticket
aliases: add a deadline to a ticket
body:
Tickets past their due date show a red clock in views.
1. Open the ticket.
2. In the **Properties** panel, select **Due date**.
3. Pick a date from the calendar.
4. Select **Save**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Forward a ticket by email
aliases: send a ticket to someone outside Harbour Desk
email a ticket to a supplier
share a ticket with a third party
body:
A note is added to the ticket recording who it was forwarded to.
1. Open the ticket.
2. Select the **More actions** menu, then **Forward by email**.
3. Enter the recipient's address and edit the message if needed.
4. Select **Send**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Link a ticket to a problem ticket
aliases: connect tickets to a known issue
body:
When you solve the problem ticket you can solve all linked tickets in one step.
1. Open the ticket.
2. In the **Properties** panel, select **Link to problem**.
3. Search for the problem ticket by number or subject.
4. Select it, then select **Save**.

title: Change the requester on a ticket
aliases: switch who the ticket is from
body:
Future replies go to the new requester.
1. Open the ticket.
2. In the **Properties** panel, select the name under **Requester**.
3. Select **Change requester** and search for the correct customer.
4. Select them, then select **Save**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Add a new requester
body:
1. Go to **Requesters** in the left menu.
2. Select **Add requester**.
3. Enter the **Name** and **Email**.
4. Add a **Phone** number and **Organisation** if you have them.
5. Select **Save**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Update a requester's phone number
aliases: new phone number for a customer
body:
1. Go to **Requesters** and search for the person.
2. Open their profile.
3. Select **Edit** beside **Phone**.
4. Enter the new number, including the area code.
5. Select **Save**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Change a requester's primary email address
body:
The old address is kept as a secondary identity so existing tickets stay linked.
1. Go to **Requesters** and open the person's profile.
2. Select **Edit** in the **Contact details** panel.
3. Enter the new address in **Email**.
4. Select **Save**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Add a secondary email address to a requester
aliases: add another email for a customer
body:
Tickets sent from any of the person's addresses will be linked to this profile.
1. Open the requester's profile from **Requesters**.
2. Select **Add email** under **Contact details**.
3. Enter the additional address.
4. Select **Save**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Delete a requester
body:
Their tickets are kept, but the requester name is shown as **Deleted user**.
1. Go to **Requesters** and open the person's profile.
2. Select the **More actions** menu.
3. Select **Delete requester**.
4. Select **Delete** to confirm.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Merge duplicate requesters
body:
Tickets and email addresses from the duplicate move to the profile you keep. This cannot be undone.
1. Open the profile you want to keep.
2. Select the **More actions** menu, then **Merge**.
3. Search for the duplicate requester and select them.
4. Select **Merge requesters**.

title: Import requesters from a CSV file
body:
The file must include an **Email** column. You will be emailed a summary when the import finishes.
1. Go to **Requesters**, then select **Import**.
2. Select **Choose file** and pick your CSV.
3. Match each column to a field, such as **Name** and **Email**.
4. Select **Start import**.

title: Export requesters to CSV
aliases: get all contacts in a spreadsheet
body:
Only admins can export requesters.
1. Go to **Requesters**.
2. Select **Export**.
3. Choose the fields to include.
4. Select **Export to CSV**, then download the file from the email we send you.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Add a note to a requester's profile
aliases: write a note on a customer
add a comment to a contact
body:
Notes appear next to every ticket from this person, and only agents can see them.
1. Open the requester's profile.
2. Select the **Notes** box in the side panel.
3. Type your note.
4. Select outside the box to save it.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Create an organisation
body:
1. Go to **Organisations** in the left menu.
2. Select **Add organisation**.
3. Enter the **Name**.
4. Add a **Domain**, **Address** and **Notes** if needed.
5. Select **Save**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Add a requester to an organisation
aliases: put a customer in a company
assign a contact to an organisation
link a person to a client
body:
A requester can belong to one organisation at a time.
1. Open the requester's profile.
2. Select **Edit** beside **Organisation**.
3. Search for the organisation and select it.
4. Select **Save**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Remove a requester from an organisation
aliases: take a customer out of a company
unlink a person from an organisation
body:
1. Open the requester's profile.
2. Select **Edit** beside **Organisation**.
3. Select the **x** next to the organisation name.
4. Select **Save**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it. If you cannot see this option, ask an admin to check your role permissions.

title: Rename an organisation
body:
Existing tickets show the new name straight away.
1. Go to **Organisations** and open the organisation.
2. Select **Edit** at the top of the profile.
3. Change the **Name**.
4. Select **Save**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Delete an organisation
body:
Its requesters are kept but no longer belong to an organisation.
1. Go to **Organisations** and open the organisation.
2. Select the **More actions** menu.
3. Select **Delete organisation**.
4. Select **Delete** to confirm.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Assign requesters to an organisation by email domain
aliases: match contacts to companies by email
body:
Only new requesters are matched. Existing requesters stay as they are.
1. Open the organisation from **Organisations**.
2. Select **Edit**.
3. Enter the email domain, for example **example.com.au**, in **Domains**.
4. Tick **Add new requesters automatically**.
5. Select **Save**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Block a requester
body:
Emails from blocked requesters do not create tickets. To undo this, select **Unblock requester** from the same menu.
1. Open the requester's profile.
2. Select the **More actions** menu.
3. Select **Block requester**.
4. Select **Block** to confirm.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: View a requester's ticket history
aliases: see all tickets from a customer
body:
1. Go to **Requesters** and open the person's profile.
2. Select the **Tickets** tab.
3. Use the **Status** filter to show open, solved or all tickets.
4. Select a ticket to open it.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Set a requester's language and time zone
body:
Automatic replies and due dates use these settings.
1. Open the requester's profile.
2. Select **Edit** in the **Contact details** panel.
3. Choose a **Language** and **Time zone** from the lists.
4. Select **Save**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Set an organisation's billing contact
aliases: change the primary contact for a company
body:
The billing contact is shown at the top of the organisation profile.
1. Open the organisation from **Organisations**.
2. Select the **Requesters** tab.
3. Select the **More** menu beside the person.
4. Select **Set as billing contact**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Update an organisation's address
body:
1. Go to **Organisations** and open the organisation.
2. Select **Edit**.
3. Update the **Address** field.
4. Select **Save**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it. If you cannot see this option, ask an admin to check your role permissions.

title: Create a view
body:
Your new view appears in the **Views** list straight away.
1. Go to **Views** and select **Add view**.
2. Enter a **Title**.
3. Under **Conditions**, add the rules, such as **Status is Open** and **Group is Billing**.
4. Select **Save**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Edit a view
body:
1. Go to **Views** and hover over the view.
2. Select the pencil icon.
3. Change the **Title**, **Conditions** or **Columns**.
4. Select **Save**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Delete a view
aliases: get rid of a saved list
body:
Deleting a view does not delete any of the tickets in it.
1. Go to **Views** and hover over the view.
2. Select the pencil icon.
3. Select **Delete view**.
4. Select **Delete** to confirm.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Share a view with a group
aliases: make a view available to my team
body:
Choose **All agents** to share the view with everyone. Only admins can share views with all agents.
1. Go to **Views** and open the view's edit page.
2. Under **Available to**, choose **Group** and select the group.
3. Select **Save**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Change the order of views
aliases: put a view at the top
body:
1. Go to **Views** and select **Manage views**.
2. Drag a view by the handle on its left.
3. Drop it where you want it.
4. Select **Save order**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Add a column to a view
aliases: show another field in a ticket list
body:
Drag columns to change their order.
1. Go to **Views** and open the view's edit page.
2. Under **Columns**, select **Add column**.
3. Choose the field, such as **Organisation** or **Priority**.
4. Select **Save**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Change how a view is sorted
body:
To keep a sort order every time, set **Order by** on the view's edit page.
1. Go to **Views** and open the view.
2. Select a column heading, such as **Updated**, to sort by it.
3. Select the heading again to switch between ascending and descending.

title: Export a view to CSV
aliases: save a ticket list as a spreadsheet
body:
The file includes the columns shown in the view, up to 5,000 tickets.
1. Go to **Views** and open the view.
2. Select the **More actions** menu.
3. Select **Export to CSV**.
4. Download the file from the email we send you.

title: Search tickets by keyword
body:
1. Select the **Search** box at the top of the screen.
2. Type a word or phrase from the subject or message.
3. Press **Enter**.
4. Select **Tickets** to see ticket results only.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Search for tickets from an email address
body:
1. Select the **Search** box.
2. Type **requester:** followed by the email address, for example **requester:sam@example.com.au**.
3. Press **Enter**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it. If you cannot see this option, ask an admin to check your role permissions.

title: Search tickets by date range
body:
1. Select the **Search** box and enter your keywords, if any.
2. Select **Filters** on the results page.
3. Choose **Created** or **Updated**, then pick **From** and **To** dates.
4. Select **Apply**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Save a search as a view
aliases: turn a search into a view
body:
The new view appears under **My views** and updates as tickets change.
1. Run your search and set any filters.
2. Select **Save as view** above the results.
3. Enter a **Title**.
4. Select **Save**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Search tickets by tag
body:
Add a minus sign before the word, such as **-tags:refund**, to leave those tickets out.
1. Select the **Search** box.
2. Type **tags:** followed by the tag, for example **tags:refund**.
3. Press **Enter**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Search tickets by status
body:
Use **status<solved** to find tickets that are not yet solved.
1. Select the **Search** box.
2. Type **status:** followed by the status, for example **status:pending**.
3. Press **Enter**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Search for an exact phrase
body:
Without quotation marks, results include tickets containing any of the words.
1. Select the **Search** box.
2. Type your phrase inside double quotation marks, for example **"refund request"**.
3. Press **Enter**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Search for an organisation
body:
1. Select the **Search** box at the top of the screen.
2. Type the organisation's name or domain.
3. Press **Enter**, then select **Organisations**.
4. Select the organisation to open it.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Search for a requester by phone number
body:
Phone numbers must match exactly, so try the number with and without the leading zero if you get no results.
1. Go to **Requesters**.
2. Select the search box above the list.
3. Enter the phone number without spaces.
4. Press **Enter**.

title: Clear your recent searches
body:
This only affects your own search history.
1. Select the **Search** box.
2. Select **Clear recent searches** below the list.
3. Select **Clear** to confirm.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Set your default view
body:
1. Select your profile picture, then **Preferences**.
2. Under **Agent workspace**, find **Default view**.
3. Choose a view from the list.
4. Select **Save**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Duplicate a view
aliases: make a copy of a view
base a new view on an existing one
body:
1. Go to **Views** and hover over the view.
2. Select the pencil icon.
3. Select **Clone**.
4. Rename the copy, adjust the conditions if needed, then select **Save**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Add a tag to a ticket
aliases: put a keyword on a ticket
body:
Tags are lower case and cannot contain spaces. Use hyphens instead.
1. Open the ticket.
2. In the **Properties** panel, select the **Tags** field.
3. Type a tag and press **Enter**. Repeat for more tags.
4. Select **Save**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Remove a tag from a ticket
aliases: delete a tag from one ticket
body:
1. Open the ticket.
2. In the **Properties** panel, find the **Tags** field.
3. Select the **x** next to the tag.
4. Select **Save**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Rename a tag
body:
Every ticket with the old tag is updated.
1. Go to **Admin**, then **Tags**.
2. Find the tag in the list.
3. Select **Rename**.
4. Enter the new name and select **Save**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Delete a tag
aliases: erase a label from all tickets
body:
The tag is removed from all tickets that use it.
1. Go to **Admin**, then **Tags**.
2. Find the tag in the list.
3. Select **Delete**.
4. Select **Delete tag** to confirm.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Add a tag to many tickets at once
body:
1. Open a view or search results.
2. Tick the checkbox next to each ticket.
3. Select **Bulk edit**, then **Add tags**.
4. Enter the tag and select **Submit**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: See how often each tag is used
body:
1. Go to **Admin**, then **Tags**.
2. Read the **Tickets** column to see how many tickets use each tag.
3. Select a column heading to sort the list.
4. Select a tag name to open a search for its tickets.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Set the priority on a ticket
aliases: mark a ticket as high priority
body:
1. Open the ticket.
2. In the **Properties** panel, select the **Priority** field.
3. Choose **Low**, **Normal**, **High** or **Urgent**.
4. Select **Save**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Escalate a ticket to urgent
body:
Urgent tickets appear at the top of the **Urgent now** view.
1. Open the ticket.
2. Set **Priority** to **Urgent** in the **Properties** panel.
3. Select **Add note** and explain why the ticket is urgent.
4. Mention your team lead with @ and their name.
5. Select **Add note**.

title: Change the default priority for new tickets
body:
This applies to new tickets created by email or the web form.
1. Go to **Admin**, then **Settings**, then **Tickets**.
2. Find **Default priority**.
3. Choose **Low** or **Normal**.
4. Select **Save**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Rename a priority level
body:
Only the display name changes. Search still uses the original name.
1. Go to **Admin**, then **Settings**, then **Priorities**.
2. Select **Edit** beside the priority.
3. Enter the new **Display name**.
4. Select **Save**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Change a ticket's status
aliases: move a ticket to another status
body:
1. Open the ticket.
2. Select the arrow beside the **Submit** button.
3. Choose the status, such as **Open** or **Pending**.
4. Select **Submit**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Create a custom status
aliases: new status like waiting on supplier
body:
The category decides how the status behaves in reports and automations.
1. Go to **Admin**, then **Settings**, then **Statuses**.
2. Select **Add status**.
3. Enter a **Name** and choose a **Category**, such as **Pending** or **On hold**.
4. Pick a colour.
5. Select **Save**.

title: Edit a custom status
body:
Standard statuses such as **Open** and **Closed** cannot be renamed.
1. Go to **Admin**, then **Settings**, then **Statuses**.
2. Select **Edit** beside the status.
3. Change the **Name** or **Description**.
4. Select **Save**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Delete a custom status
body:
1. Go to **Admin**, then **Settings**, then **Statuses**.
2. Select **Delete** beside the custom status.
3. Choose a replacement status for tickets that currently use it.
4. Select **Delete status**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Put a ticket on hold
body:
Use on hold when you are waiting on someone inside your organisation. Use **Pending** when you are waiting on the customer.
1. Open the ticket.
2. Select the arrow beside the **Submit** button.
3. Choose **On hold**.
4. Select **Submit**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Set a ticket to pending
body:
If the customer replies, the ticket changes back to **Open** automatically.
1. Open the ticket and select **Reply**.
2. Write your message asking for more information.
3. Select the arrow beside **Submit** and choose **Pending**.
4. Select **Send**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Mark a ticket as solved
body:
Solved tickets close automatically after the period set in **Settings**.
1. Open the ticket.
2. Write a final reply if needed.
3. Select the arrow beside **Submit** and choose **Solved**.
4. Select **Send**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Change when solved tickets close automatically
body:
1. Go to **Admin**, then **Settings**, then **Tickets**.
2. Find **Close solved tickets after**.
3. Enter a number of days between 1 and 28.
4. Select **Save**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Add tags automatically based on keywords
aliases: set up a rule to label tickets
body:
1. Go to **Admin**, then **Automations**, then **Triggers**.
2. Select **Add trigger** and enter a name.
3. Under **Conditions**, choose **Subject or description contains** and enter the keyword.
4. Under **Actions**, choose **Add tags** and enter the tag.
5. Select **Save**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Change the colour of a status
aliases: make statuses easier to tell apart
body:
1. Go to **Admin**, then **Settings**, then **Statuses**.
2. Select **Edit** beside the status.
3. Select the **Colour** swatch and choose a new colour.
4. Select **Save**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Create a macro
body:
A macro applies several changes to a ticket in one click.
1. Go to **Admin**, then **Macros**.
2. Select **Add macro**.
3. Enter a **Title** that agents will recognise.
4. Under **Actions**, add the actions you want, such as **Comment text** or **Set status**.
5. Select **Create**.

title: Edit a macro
body:
1. Go to **Admin**, then **Macros**.
2. Find the macro and select **Edit**.
3. Change the **Title** or **Actions**.
4. Select **Save**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it. If you cannot see this option, ask an admin to check your role permissions.

title: Delete a macro
body:
Tickets already updated by the macro are not affected.
1. Go to **Admin**, then **Macros**.
2. Select the **More** menu beside the macro.
3. Select **Delete**.
4. Select **Delete macro** to confirm.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Apply a macro to a ticket
body:
1. Open the ticket.
2. Select **Apply macro** below the reply box.
3. Search for the macro or pick it from the list.
4. Check the reply and properties it fills in, edit as needed, then select **Submit**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Apply a macro to several tickets
aliases: use a macro on multiple tickets
body:
Macros that add a public reply send it to every requester.
1. Open a view and tick the checkbox next to each ticket.
2. Select **Bulk edit**, then **Apply macro**.
3. Choose the macro.
4. Select **Submit**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Make a macro available to all agents
body:
To share with one team only, choose **Group** instead.
1. Go to **Admin**, then **Macros**.
2. Select **Edit** beside the macro.
3. Under **Available for**, choose **All agents**.
4. Select **Save**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Create a personal macro
aliases: make a macro just for me
body:
Only you can see and use a personal macro.
1. Select your profile picture, then **My macros**.
2. Select **Add macro**.
3. Enter a **Title** and add your actions.
4. Select **Create**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Add the requester's name to a macro
body:
The placeholder is replaced with the customer's first name when the macro is applied.
1. Open the macro from **Admin**, then **Macros**.
2. In the **Comment text** action, place your cursor where the name should appear.
3. Type **{{ticket.requester.first_name}}**.
4. Select **Save**.

title: Set a status in a macro
body:
1. Open the macro from **Admin**, then **Macros**.
2. Under **Actions**, select **Add action**.
3. Choose **Set status** and pick the status, such as **Solved**.
4. Select **Save**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Add a tag in a macro
aliases: put a tag action in a macro
body:
1. Open the macro from **Admin**, then **Macros**.
2. Select **Add action**.
3. Choose **Add tags** and enter the tag.
4. Select **Save**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Deactivate a macro
body:
Deactivated macros are kept under **Inactive** and can be turned back on with **Activate**.
1. Go to **Admin**, then **Macros**.
2. Select the **More** menu beside the macro.
3. Select **Deactivate**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Duplicate a macro
aliases: reuse a macro as a template
body:
1. Go to **Admin**, then **Macros**.
2. Select the **More** menu beside the macro.
3. Select **Clone**.
4. Rename the copy and select **Create**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Organise macros into categories
body:
Macros with the same category name appear together in the **Apply macro** list.
1. Open the macro from **Admin**, then **Macros**.
2. In the **Title** field, type a category name followed by two colons, then the macro name, for example **Billing::Refund approved**.
3. Select **Save**.

title: Find a macro
body:
Inside a ticket, select **Apply macro** and type in the search box to find it.
1. Go to **Admin**, then **Macros**.
2. Type part of the macro's title in the search box.
3. Select **Edit** to view its actions.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Save a canned reply
body:
Unlike macros, canned replies only insert text and do not change ticket properties.
1. Go to **Admin**, then **Canned replies**.
2. Select **Add canned reply**.
3. Enter a **Name** and the **Message**.
4. Choose who it is **Available to**.
5. Select **Save**.

title: Insert a canned reply into a ticket
body:
1. Open the ticket and select **Reply**.
2. Select the **Canned replies** icon above the message box, or type **/** in the box.
3. Search for the reply and select it.
4. Edit the text if needed, then select **Send**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Edit a canned reply
body:
1. Go to **Admin**, then **Canned replies**.
2. Select the reply's name.
3. Change the **Name** or **Message**.
4. Select **Save**.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it. If you cannot see this option, ask an admin to check your role permissions.

title: Delete a canned reply
body:
1. Go to **Admin**, then **Canned replies**.
2. Select the **More** menu beside the reply.
3. Select **Delete**.
4. Select **Delete reply** to confirm.
Your change takes effect immediately and is recorded in the audit log, so admins can see who made it.

title: Add an attachment to a macro
aliases: send a file with a macro
attach a document to a macro
include a PDF in a macro
body:
Files can be up to 7 MB. The file is attached to the public reply when the macro is applied.
1. Open the macro from **Admin**, then **Macros**.
2. Under **Actions**, select **Add action**, then **Attachment**.
3. Select **Upload file** and choose the file.
4. Select **Save**.

title: See how often a macro is used
body:
Macros that are never used are good candidates for deactivating.
1. Go to **Admin**, then **Macros**.
2. Select **Usage** at the top of the list.
3. Choose a period, such as **Last 30 days**.
4. Sort by **Times used** to see the most popular macros.
